name: apktool
desc: Tool for reverse engineering 3rd party, closed, binary Android apps
why: Decodes closed Android APKs into smali and resources, a solid door into how apps are taken apart, though fairly well known.

brief.what_it_is: Apktool is a command-line tool for reverse engineering closed, binary Android apps. You give it an APK file and it decodes the resources and manifest to nearly their original form and disassembles the code into smali, which lays the app out as a project folder. After you edit that folder, the same tool rebuilds it into an APK. The homepage transcript shows version 3.0.3 in use.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it as a way to take third-party, closed Android apps apart so people can inspect and modify them, for example to localize an app or add features. It also says it is not for piracy.
brief.how_it_works: Running decode (d) on an APK writes out a project-like folder with decoded resources, manifest and smali code, and it copies unknown and original files across. Running build (b) on that folder reassembles the smali into classes.dex, rebuilds the resources and packages a new APK. The homepage also describes an analyze mode: attaching -m to a decode command skips rebuilding and just unpacks resources and manifest for inspection.

commands_seen.context: Decodes the APK test.apk into a folder of resources and smali (the disassemble step, shown on the homepage transcript).
Rebuilds the decoded folder test into a new APK (the assemble step, shown on the homepage transcript).

brief.install_notes: The fetched text does not include install steps beyond the download links. The README points to Bitbucket and a mirror for downloads and to a 'How to Build' page at apktool.org/docs/build, which I did not fetch, so any Java runtime or build requirements are unverified. The brew entry gives the executable name as apktool.
brief.standout: Unlike a plain decompiler, it aims to round-trip: you can decode, change resources or smali, and rebuild a working APK, with a project-style layout and automation for repetitive steps. The smali output also lets you step through app code.
brief.status: Appears maintained, though I could not confirm a date. The homepage shows version 3.0.3, the GitHub README has a CI badge and describes a 'main' branch for 3.x plus a 2.x maintenance branch. I saw no release date or last commit date.
brief.caveats: The README says Apktool is NOT intended for piracy and other non-legal uses. Decoding is 'nearly original', not exact, so rebuilt output may not match the source. Licensed under Apache 2.0, per the README badge. Downloads are linked from Bitbucket and a personal mirror rather than GitHub releases. Platform support and build difficulty were not stated in the text I read.
quotes: Apktool is a tool for reverse engineering third-party, closed, binary, Android apps.
It can decode resources to nearly original form and rebuild them after making some modifications; it makes it possible to debug smali code step-by-step.
Just try to be fair with the authors of an app, that you use and probably like.
